## Baseline

- Schema version: 1.0
- Last reviewed: 2026-09-24
- Documentation baseline: Google Cloud Spanner public documentation reviewed 2026-08-25
- Targeted update: 2026-09-28; closed the developer-usability plan (docs/plans/2026-09-27-usability-closure-plan.md): every former partial, unsupported, and unknown record was re-evaluated after implementation, and physical properties were split into not-applicable records. Evidence tiers: native unit and native conformance (fixed-environment Bazel full suite, 159/159 targets), native --data_dir restart probe, and native public-endpoint client matrix and doc-example run on the final binaries; the packaged Docker/LocalCloud image was not qualified. A second targeted update on 2026-09-28 applied three remaining-limitations batches (graph algorithms, search tokenization and scoring, resume tokens, wound-wait lock waits, persisted SPANNER_SYS statistics and new SPANNER_SYS tables, FGAC checks, PostgreSQL search and vector index DDL output, max_commit_delay validation, ListOperations filters, change stream retention cleanup, the persistent-storage range-scan fix, and the --data_dir lock). It re-ran only the native unit and conformance tiers (combined fixed-environment native suite, 164/164 targets on bd6a9646); the client matrix and restart probe were not re-run. A third targeted update on 2026-09-28 qualified the packaged Docker image localcloud-spanner-emulator:local across all verification tiers (tests/image_verification_test.py and tests/client_matrix/): clients.docker and emulator.packaging became tested: 138 supported, 8 accepted-no-op, 9 not-applicable. Full-inventory review remains dated 2026-09-24. A fourth targeted update on 2026-09-28 synced upstream/master v1.5.58 (a081a7e7), incorporating tables without primary keys, GoogleSQL score_version database option, PostgreSQL TABLESAMPLE (BERNOULLI and SPANNER.RESERVOIR), NULL_FILTERED with WHERE clause index validation, increased table limits (5,000 tables), and internal Queue catalog/validator schema objects.
- Upstream Emulator Revision: a081a7e7 (upstream/master v1.5.58)
- Googlesql Dependency Version: 2026.7.2

This inventory covers the major documented Spanner feature areas. It is an evolving baseline, not a claim that every individual RPC, SQL function, option, quota, or production semantic has already been independently verified. Missing detail should be added as `unknown` until evidence supports a stronger classification.

## Status legend

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `supported` | Behavior needed for local development is implemented and has representative evidence. |
| `partial` | A useful subset works, but some documented semantics or variants are missing or not yet verified. |
| `accepted-no-op` | Syntax or API input is accepted for compatibility, but documented behavior is intentionally not performed. |
| `unsupported` | Applicable to local development but not implemented. |
| `not-applicable` | Production-only behavior has no meaningful local emulator equivalent. |
| `unknown` | The audit did not find enough evidence to classify the feature safely. |

## Verification legend

| Verification | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `tested` | A cited repository test exercises at least one stated behavior; this label does not report a current test run or full feature coverage. |
| `implemented` | Implementation evidence exists, but representative behavior was not confirmed by the audit. |
| `documented` | Only project documentation supports the claim. |
| `unverified` | No reliable repository evidence was identified. |

| `data.sql.execute_streaming` | ExecuteStreamingSql RPC | `supported` | `local-development` | `googlesql`, `postgresql` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/rpc/google.spanner.v1#spanner](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/rpc/google.spanner.v1#spanner) | [frontend/handlers/queries.cc](../frontend/handlers/queries.cc)<br>[frontend/converters/chunking.cc](../frontend/converters/chunking.cc)<br>[frontend/converters/resume_tokens.cc](../frontend/converters/resume_tokens.cc)<br>[frontend/proto/resume_token.proto](../frontend/proto/resume_token.proto)<br>[frontend/handlers/queries_test.cc](../frontend/handlers/queries_test.cc)<br>[frontend/converters/chunking_test.cc](../frontend/converters/chunking_test.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/query_modes.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/query_modes.cc)<br>[frontend/converters/resume_tokens_test.cc](../frontend/converters/resume_tokens_test.cc) | `tested` | Results stream as PartialResultSets of whole rows, each response at most 1 MB; a row larger than that is split across responses with chunked_value. The query plan comes with the stream and statistics on its last message. Responses that end on a row boundary carry a resume token (request fingerprint, transaction or single-use read timestamp, row count and a fingerprint of the rows sent); a request resent with the token re-executes in the same transaction or at the same read timestamp and continues after that row. A garbled token, a token from a different request, or a resent request that begins a new transaction returns INVALID_ARGUMENT, and rows that differ on re-execution (a nondeterministic result such as RAND()) return FAILED_PRECONDITION. DML streams carry no resume tokens. |
| `data.sql.partition_query` | PartitionQuery RPC | `supported` | `local-development` | `googlesql`, `postgresql` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/rpc/google.spanner.v1#spanner](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/rpc/google.spanner.v1#spanner) | [frontend/handlers/partitions.cc](../frontend/handlers/partitions.cc)<br>[backend/query/partitionability_validator.cc](../backend/query/partitionability_validator.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/partition_query.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/partition_query.cc)<br>[backend/query/partitionability_validator_test.cc](../backend/query/partitionability_validator_test.cc) | `tested` | PartitionQuery requires a read-only transaction and returns tokens that are only valid with the same session, transaction, SQL, and parameters. Queries that production cannot root-partition (ORDER BY, some subqueries, multi-table scans) are rejected. The response always has exactly two partitions, one empty and one with every row, so it does not model real parallelism or partition_options. |

UpdateBackup accepts only future expire_time and CopyBackup enforces its minimum retention from the request time. Schema, grants, and saved sequence counters (including identity columns) are restored; row deletion policies are dropped from the restored database, as Spanner documents. encryption_config accepts the Google-default types. The first schema batch receives the restore time, so change-stream start timestamps before the restore are not guaranteed to work. Ordinary failures roll back the target; a failed rollback can require restart reconciliation. |
| `backups.schedules` | Backup schedule RPCs | `supported` | `local-development` | `api` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/rpc/google.spanner.admin.database.v1](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/reference/rpc/google.spanner.admin.database.v1) | [frontend/handlers/backups.cc](../frontend/handlers/backups.cc)<br>[frontend/persistence/backup_catalog.cc](../frontend/persistence/backup_catalog.cc)<br>[binaries/emulator_main.cc](../binaries/emulator_main.cc)<br>[frontend/handlers/backups_test.cc](../frontend/handlers/backups_test.cc)<br>[frontend/persistence/backup_catalog_test.cc](../frontend/persistence/backup_catalog_test.cc)<br>[docs/persistence.md](../docs/persistence.md) | `tested` | Backup schedule create, get, list, update (update_mask required), and delete persist with --data_dir. The native worker runs 12-hour, daily, weekly, and monthly UTC cron schedules, creates each due backup once, applies retention from capture time, and persists its cursor. Incremental schedules produce backups linked by incremental_backup_chain_id and oldest_version_time with freeable and exclusive size fields, but each is physically a full snapshot. Frequency limits, at most 4 schedules per database, and Google-default encryption types are enforced; customer-managed keys return UNIMPLEMENTED. Schedule-update races are guarded by a catalog compare-and-swap. |

ON ... in PostgreSQL can be added, replaced and dropped and appear in INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES and GetDatabaseDdl. A per-database sweeper deletes expired rows in batched system transactions tagged RowDeletionPolicy with is_system_transaction set, so change streams record them and exclude_ttl_deletes filters them. The sweep runs every --row_deletion_policy_sweep_interval_seconds (default 60; 0 disables), whereas production deletes within about 72 hours; a sweep batch can contend with, and abort, a user transaction. SPANNER_SYS.ROW_DELETION_POLICIES reports each table's last sweep (processed watermark, undeletable rows), and with --data_dir it survives restarts. Restore drops the policies. |

GoogleSQL and PostgreSQL change-stream tests capture UUID records; the PostgreSQL case checks INSERT/UPDATE key and value JSON plus UUID type metadata. ### DML, mutations, and batch operations

| ID | Feature | Status | Applicability | Dialects | Docs | Evidence | Verification | Notes |

| `writes.batch_dml` | Batch DML | `supported` | `local-development` | `googlesql`, `postgresql` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/dml-syntax](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/dml-syntax) | [frontend/handlers/queries.cc](../frontend/handlers/queries.cc)<br>[backend/query/query_engine.cc](../backend/query/query_engine.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/batch_dml.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/batch_dml.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/dml_replay.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/dml_replay.cc) | `tested` | ExecuteBatchDml runs statements in order and stops at the first failure, returning its status and the row counts of the statements before it; the transaction stays usable (batch_dml.cc InvalidDmlFailsButCommitSucceeds). Empty batches and queries inside a batch are rejected, it fails in read-only transactions, and batches are replay-safe by sequence number (dml_replay.cc). |
| `writes.batch_write` | BatchWrite RPC | `supported` | `local-development` | `api` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/dml-syntax](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/dml-syntax) | [frontend/handlers/batch.cc](../frontend/handlers/batch.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/batch_write.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/batch_write.cc)<br>[frontend/handlers/batch_test.cc](../frontend/handlers/batch_test.cc) | `tested` | BatchWrite commits each mutation group atomically in its own single-use read-write transaction. It processes groups sequentially and streams one response per group with that group's commit timestamp or error; a failed group does not stop later groups. This deterministic order and response grouping are allowed by Spanner's unspecified-order API contract. exclude_txn_from_change_streams is implemented, though no dedicated cited test covers it; distributed throughput is not modeled. |

| `transactions.concurrency_model` | Concurrency, aborts, and fault injection | `supported` | `local-development` | `api` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/transactions](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/transactions) | [backend/locking/manager.cc](../backend/locking/manager.cc)<br>[backend/transaction/read_write_transaction.cc](../backend/transaction/read_write_transaction.cc)<br>[common/config.cc](../common/config.cc)<br>[backend/locking/handle.cc](../backend/locking/handle.cc)<br>[backend/locking/manager_test.cc](../backend/locking/manager_test.cc)<br>[backend/database/database_test.cc](../backend/database/database_test.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/batch_dml.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/batch_dml.cc)<br>[backend/transaction/read_write_transaction_test.cc](../backend/transaction/read_write_transaction_test.cc)<br>[gateway/gateway_test.go](../gateway/gateway_test.go)<br>[README.md](../README.md) | `tested` | Key/range shared and exclusive locks let disjoint read-write transactions commit concurrently. Conflicts follow wound-wait: a younger transaction waits up to --lock_wait_timeout_ms (default 10000, forwarded by gateway_main; 0 restores abort-at-once) for a lock an older transaction holds and then aborts with ABORTED, and an older requester aborts (wounds) a younger holder. In a two-key deadlock exactly one transaction aborts, and an aborted requester releases its locks at once. Focused manager and transaction tests cover waits, wounds, timeouts, disjoint ranges and tables, read upgrade, lock cleanup, abort/retry, deadlock, and a 5,000-row insert performance gate. --abort_current_transaction_probability (default 20, emulator_main only) lets a younger requester sometimes abort an idle older holder instead of waiting; schema changes never wait. SPANNER_SYS.LOCK_STATS reports the measured waits. --enable_fault_injection aborts about 5% of first commit attempts. Differences: waits ignore the RPC deadline, idle transactions are not aborted after 10 seconds, and READ_STATS AVG_LOCKING_DELAY_SECONDS stays 0. |

Constraint checks still use the latest data. Partitioned DML rejects REPEATABLE_READ. Read-only transactions accept either option. |

Churn is timer-driven (normally after 20-40 seconds), not load-driven, and all writes go to the active partition whose token sorts first; other active partitions produce only heartbeat and child-partition records. Each churn cycle also deletes data change records older than the stream's retention period (none are deleted with --enable_change_stream_churning=false). The token lifetime can be shortened with --override_change_stream_partition_token_alive_seconds. Initial partitions are not duplicated after restart with --data_dir. |
| `change_streams.read` | Read change stream | `supported` | `local-development` | — | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/change-streams](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/change-streams) | [frontend/handlers/change_streams.cc](../frontend/handlers/change_streams.cc)<br>[backend/query/change_stream/change_stream_query_validator.cc](../backend/query/change_stream/change_stream_query_validator.cc)<br>[backend/transaction/transaction_store.cc](../backend/transaction/transaction_store.cc)<br>[frontend/entities/transaction.cc](../frontend/entities/transaction.cc)<br>[common/change_stream.cc](../common/change_stream.cc)<br>[frontend/converters/change_streams.cc](../frontend/converters/change_streams.cc)<br>[frontend/proto/resume_token.proto](../frontend/proto/resume_token.proto)<br>[frontend/handlers/change_streams_test.cc](../frontend/handlers/change_streams_test.cc)<br>[backend/query/change_stream/change_stream_query_validator_test.cc](../backend/query/change_stream/change_stream_query_validator_test.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/change_streams_read_write.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/change_streams_read_write.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/pg_change_streams_read_write.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/pg_change_streams_read_write.cc)<br>[frontend/converters/change_streams_test.cc](../frontend/converters/change_streams_test.cc)<br>[frontend/converters/pg_change_streams_test.cc](../frontend/converters/pg_change_streams_test.cc)<br>[docs/change-streams.md](../docs/change-streams.md) | `tested` | READ_<stream> queries return data change, heartbeat, and child partition records; start_timestamp is checked against the retention period and the stream's creation time, which survives restarts and restores. DML UPDATE records only the key, SET, commit-timestamp and ON UPDATE columns, so records match Update mutations; REPLACE of an existing row emits DELETE then INSERT. TTL deletes carry the RowDeletionPolicy tag with is_system_transaction set; user transactions report an empty transaction_tag and number_of_partitions_in_transaction 1. Resume tokens encode the partition token, commit timestamp and record index (fork; they were placeholders before), and a query resent with one skips the records already returned. Records past the retention period are deleted on each partition churner cycle, so deletion lags by up to one pass (never with --enable_change_stream_churning=false). In-flight queries do not survive restart. A pre-existing scan-window boundary issue can skip a commit that falls exactly on a window's microsecond boundary (see docs/known-gaps.md). |

NULL inputs return SQL NULL. DEBUG_TOKENLIST matches both documented examples; TOKENLISTs stored by earlier builds lack its boundary and hashtag markers. PostgreSQL spanner.tokenize_substring passed its arguments in the wrong order and crashed with relative_search_types; it now works and also takes support_relative_search. Residual difference: the ICU build has no CJK dictionaries, so Chinese, Japanese and Korean text is split only where the script changes and pure Chinese text is not segmented into words. |

| ID | Feature | Status | Applicability | Dialects | Docs | Evidence | Verification | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `graph.algorithms` | Graph algorithms | `supported` | `local-development` | `googlesql` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/graph/overview](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/graph/overview) | [backend/query/graph/graph_algorithms.cc](../backend/query/graph/graph_algorithms.cc)<br>[backend/query/graph/graph_algorithm_table_valued_function.cc](../backend/query/graph/graph_algorithm_table_valued_function.cc)<br>[frontend/handlers/queries.cc](../frontend/handlers/queries.cc)<br>[build/bazel/googlesql.patch](../build/bazel/googlesql.patch)<br>[backend/query/query_engine_test.cc](../backend/query/query_engine_test.cc)<br>[backend/query/graph/graph_algorithms_test.cc](../backend/query/graph/graph_algorithms_test.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/graph_algorithms.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/graph_algorithms.cc)<br>[README.md](../README.md) | `tested` | All 13 documented algorithms are computed in memory: PageRank (including personalized), BetweennessCentrality, ClosenessCentrality, WeaklyConnectedComponents, ModularityClustering, CorrelationClustering, LabelPropagation, CliqueFinding, JaccardSimilarity, CosineSimilarity, CommonNeighborsSimilarity, TotalNeighborsSimilarity and ShortestPath (path and cost). They take the documented named arguments and are called with GRAPH g CALL Algo(...) YIELD over the whole graph or with CALL PER () over the rows of the preceding query (including a FULL UNION ALL of nodes and edges), yielding graph nodes, paths and the documented columns; ELEMENT_DEFINITION_NAME works in the calling statement. The documented PageRank example returns the documented results. EXPORT DATA runs its query: format CLOUD_SPANNER writes the rows back to Spanner tables (update_ignore_all / upsert_ignore_all; rows that violate constraints are skipped), and CSV, Parquet and Avro validate their options and then discard the rows. Results are deterministic; where Spanner does not publish an algorithm's exact method they are emulator-defined. machine_category, zone and max_idle_time are validated only; algorithm permission, schema and RETURN-clause rules are not enforced; SPANNER_SYS.GRAPH_OPERATION_EXECUTION_STATUS is not populated; and a write-back inside a read-write transaction can conflict with that transaction's own locks. GoogleSQL only. Formerly accepted-no-op (zero-argument stand-ins). |

GoogleSQL only. |
| `graph.gql_queries` | GQL queries | `supported` | `local-development` | `googlesql` | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/graph/overview](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/graph/overview) | [backend/query/queryable_property_graph.cc](../backend/query/queryable_property_graph.cc)<br>[backend/query/query_engine.cc](../backend/query/query_engine.cc)<br>[backend/query/query_engine_test.cc](../backend/query/query_engine_test.cc)<br>[tests/conformance/cases/query.cc](../tests/conformance/cases/query.cc)<br>[README.md](../README.md) | `tested` | GQL queries (GRAPH ... The full GQL surface comes from GoogleSQL and is not exhaustively tested. Known pre-existing bug: ORDER BY in RETURN ... ORDER BY is ignored, and rows come back in the emulator's random order (query_engine_test pins the unsorted results; see docs/known-gaps.md). |

SPLIT and recommendation tables exist and are empty. Only closed intervals are shown unless --spanner_sys_expose_open_interval is set, as production shows only ended intervals. With a database role, SPANNER_SYS requires spanner_sys_reader. LOCK_STATS LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS and TOTAL_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS report measured wound-wait lock waits. With --data_dir the interval statistics, table size samples and last TTL sweeps persist per database (spanner_sys_statistics.json, saved when a minute interval ends and on SIGTERM/SIGINT; a crash loses up to the current minute; dropping the database deletes the file), and split points persist with the database data. Differences: text fingerprints differ from production; physical columns (memory, disk I/O and similar) and READ_STATS AVG_LOCKING_DELAY_SECONDS are zero; TABLE_SIZES_STATS_1HOUR averages a logical size estimate sampled every 5 minutes (USED_HDD_BYTES 0); ACTIVE_PARTITIONED_DMLS shows one partition with progress 0 until the statement finishes; QUERY_PROFILES_TOP*, TASKS and TABLE_SIZES_STATS_PER_LOCALITY_GROUP_1HOUR are absent. |

IN SCHEMA) and role membership work in both dialects. Grants are validated, printed by GetDatabaseDdl, replayed from --data_dir and backups, and revoked automatically when an object is dropped. A session with a creator_role is restricted on queries and DML, Read, mutations (Commit, BatchWrite), and change stream reads; DEFINER views need only SELECT on the view, while INVOKER view bodies are checked at analysis, including in PLAN mode. Sequences used by column defaults need their privilege, and pg_catalog rows about schema objects are filtered by role like INFORMATION_SCHEMA. Differences: error texts are the emulator's, and graph algorithm permission rules are not enforced. Sessions without a role have full access, as a principal with database-level IAM access does. |

A supplied nonempty etag must match the current policy or SetIamPolicy returns ABORTED; every successful write gets a fresh etag. Enforcement is a separate record (security.iam_enforcement). |

| `tested` | With --data_dir, row data (LevelDB, multi-version), schema contents (including roles, grants, and row deletion policies), instances, custom instance configs, instance partitions, databases, IAM policies, operations, backups (including version_time and incremental chain metadata), backup schedules, sequence counters, split points, SPANNER_SYS statistics, and change-stream creation times are persisted for restart. Metadata writes are atomic and journaled, and each commit uses one atomic LevelDB data batch. Range reads and range deletes follow the on-disk key order (length, then content) with no format change; before 2026-09-28 they could skip rows, which let duplicate unique-index keys commit and break restore (the unique-index incident). A regression test and a concurrent stress test (about half its runs failed before the fix, 30 of 30 passed after) cover it. The directory is locked with <data_dir>/.lock (flock, holder PID recorded), so a second emulator process fails at startup. Sessions, in-flight transactions and queries are transient; SPANNER_SYS statistics are saved each minute and on SIGTERM/SIGINT, so a crash loses up to the current minute. The closure's disposable process restart probe and the 2026-09-28 Docker qualification suite (tests/image_verification_test.py) confirmed roles, grants, DEFINER views, database options, TTL policies, rows, version_time backups, split points, SPANNER_SYS statistics, and directory locking across container restarts. |

The failed database is listed as CREATING and its reads, writes, and DDL return FAILED_PRECONDITION with the reason. --repair_corrupted_databases (accepted by gateway_main and emulator_main) moves its whole folder to <data_dir>/.quarantine and removes it from metadata, so later starts succeed without it. DropDatabase on it also moves it to .quarantine and frees its name; until then, CreateDatabase with that name returns ALREADY_EXISTS. |
| `emulator.startup` | Startup and ports | `supported` | `local-development` | — | [https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/emulator](https://cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/emulator) | [binaries/emulator_main.cc](../binaries/emulator_main.cc)<br>[binaries/gateway_main.go](../binaries/gateway_main.go)<br>[gateway/gateway.go](../gateway/gateway.go)<br>[common/config.cc](../common/config.cc)<br>[tests/gcloud/emulator.py](../tests/gcloud/emulator.py)<br>[gateway/gateway_test.go](../gateway/gateway_test.go)<br>[README.md](../README.md) | `tested` | gateway_main starts emulator_main and the REST proxy (defaults: --hostname localhost, --grpc_port 9010, --http_port 9020) and forwards --data_dir, --remote_functions_host_port, --repair_corrupted_databases, --log_requests, --enable_fault_injection, --disable_query_null_filtered_index_check, --enforce_placement_dml_restrictions, --override_max_databases_per_instance, --override_change_stream_partition_token_alive_seconds, --row_deletion_policy_sweep_interval_seconds, --spanner_sys_expose_open_interval, and --lock_wait_timeout_ms. --abort_current_transaction_probability and the change stream tuning flags exist only on emulator_main. On SIGINT or SIGTERM, gateway_main stops emulator_main (SIGTERM, then a kill after 5 seconds) before exiting. With --data_dir, emulator_main locks <data_dir>/.lock at startup and exits with an error naming the holder's PID if another process holds it, and on SIGINT or SIGTERM it saves SPANNER_SYS statistics before terminating. |

## Updating this file

1. Edit `docs/feature-coverage.yaml`.
2. Run `python3 tools/feature_coverage.py audit-rpcs` to confirm every registered RPC is mapped.
3. Run `python3 tools/feature_coverage.py generate`.
4. Run `python3 tools/feature_coverage.py check` and the unit tests.
